overview.text: Alameda County Community Development Agency (Economic & Civic Development Department) seeks economic development consulting for two scopes: ECD, for unincorporated communities, and the Surplus Property Authority (SPA), for property disposition. It intends a 3-year contract with an option to renew for 2 years; the estimated budget is $300,000 (2-$150,000 agreements).

summary.issuing_organization: County of Alameda; Community Development Agency, Economic & Civic Development Department; contact Marie Suvansin, (510) 670-6103, marie.suvansin@acgov.org; RFP number: Not specified in the document

scope.text: ECD: economic development services for the unincorporated communities of Castro Valley, San Lorenzo, Ashland, Cherryland, Sunol, and the rural winegrowing region of unincorporated East County.

ECD services include retail market demand and key development project analyses, innovative post-redevelopment financing approaches, support for food-related businesses, and implementation of a new economic development strategic plan.

ECD: assist with reuse of former Redevelopment Agency properties, including the historic Lorenzo Theater and 20095 Mission Boulevard; may include review of proformas for affordable housing and other developments.

SPA: assist with property disposition, including market analysis, Surplus Land Act compliance, preparing and reviewing requests for proposals, and supporting exclusive negotiation agreements and other disposition documents.
Proposers may respond to ECD only, SPA only, or both; the RFP may result in one or multiple proposers with separate agreements for ECD and SPA.
Selected proposer must create a scope and budget for specific projects as requested and attend regularly scheduled meetings set by CDA staff, where projects are determined.
Deliverables that may arise: presentations, meetings with commissions and stakeholders, and feasibility analyses of various projects.

key_requirements.text: Pass/fail: response must be complete and address all RFP requirements and addenda; failing the Proposer Minimum Qualifications may also count as an incomplete response and lead to disqualification.
Pass/fail: proposer, its principal and named subcontractors must not appear on the federal debarred, suspended or excluded parties list at www.sam.gov/SAM.

Proposer must meet the County's Small and Emerging Locally Owned Business (SLEB) requirements to be considered for award; non-certified proposers must subcontract at least 20% of the total estimated amount to a SLEB.
Proposal must include Exhibit A Response Packet in its most current version as revised by addenda; using an outdated version may lead to disqualification.
Proposer must certify it is licensed by the State of California for the work required and regularly engaged in the general class and type of work.
Proposer must certify it is not on the California DGS list of persons engaged in investment activities in Iran (Iran Contracting Act of 2010).
Contractor must provide dedicated support staff as primary contact and a dedicated, competent account manager familiar with County requirements.

Contractor must carry insurance: commercial general liability $1,000,000 per occurrence, automobile liability $1,000,000 per occurrence, workers' compensation statutory, employers liability no less than $1,000,000 per accident.
Proposals must not be marked confidential or proprietary; the County may refuse to consider any proposal or part so marked.

eligibility.text: Proposer must be regularly and continuously engaged in providing economic development consulting services for at least 5 years, clearly stated or demonstrated in the response.
Proposer must hold all permits, licenses and professional credentials needed for the services; proof is required only if the County requests it.
Proposer must be a prime contractor to the County, not a subcontractor.

Debarment and Suspension Certification: proposer, its principal and subcontractors must not be suspended, debarred or excluded by any federal agency, or indicted or convicted for fraud or official misconduct, within the past three years.
Non-certified SLEB proposers must subcontract with a certified SLEB for at least 20% of the total estimated amount to be eligible for award.
SLEB certification must be valid at the time of proposal submittal for SLEB primes and SLEB subcontractors.
Proposer must provide 3 references from public agencies or nonprofits with similar scope, and must currently serve at least two of them or have done so within the last five years.
Relevant economic development consulting work described in the proposal must fall within the prior 5 years.

commercial_requirements.text: Estimated budget for both the ECD and SPA agreements is $300,000 (2-$150,000 agreements).
Bid security, performance security and proposal fee: Not specified in the document
Liquidated damages, penalties and warranty: Not specified in the document
Cost Narrative (1 page) must explain how the proposer bills and at minimum list key personnel names and hourly rates, for the scope responded to.
County pays monthly or as agreed after invoice approval, not to exceed the total contract amount; no payment for services in advance.
County will use reasonable efforts to pay within 30 days after receipt and review of invoice and satisfactory performance.
County may withhold future payments if a review committee deems performance unsatisfactory.
Insurance certificates are not required at submission but must be provided before award, naming the County of Alameda as additional insured.

project_duration.text: By mutual agreement the contract may be extended for an additional 2-years.
During the initial 120-day period of any contract the County may review the proposal, contract and services and meet with the contractor.
Delivery milestones: Not specified in the document

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: proposals first pass a pass/fail check on completeness and debarment, then a County Selection Committee scores each criterion on a zero to five-point scale, weighted to a total.

Evaluation: Description and Understanding of Proposed Services 125 Points; Relevant Experience 125 Points; Methodology 125 Points; Proposer Interview and Reference Checks 125 Points (interviews follow a shortlist).
Evaluation: local preference 5% and small and local or emerging and local preference 5% are added; final maximum score is 550 points including 50 preference points.
Evaluation: award goes to the highest-ranked responsible proposer; combined weight of criteria outranks cost, so award may not go to the lowest price.
Submission: email all proposal documents to marie.suvansin@acgov.org by 5:00 p.m. on May 15, 2026 as PDF attachments, with the County's Response Packet pages included.
Submission: Response Packet pages not applicable must be marked N/A; signatures required on Proposer Acceptance, Debarment Certification and SLEB Information Sheet; do not modify County forms.
Submission: page limits are Team Summary 2 pages (resumes 1 page each), Cost Narrative 1 page, Description of Relevant Experience and Proposed Services 5 pages.
Submission: any exceptions or clarifications to the RFP must go on the Exceptions and Clarifications form; the County need not accept them and they may be a basis for disqualification.

Risk: Contract Start Date July 1, 2026 falls before the Board Consideration Award Date July 14, 2026, and Board approval and full execution are required before services begin; all dates are tentative.
Risk: County may terminate without cause on prior written notice, or for cause without written notice, and may seek any and all damages from the Contractor on termination with cause.

Risk: non-certified SLEB proposers need a SLEB subcontractor for at least 20%; substitutions need prior written OCCR approval; inability to meet it requires an exception that may lead to disqualification.
Risk: proposals may be disqualified for outdated Exhibit A, modified County forms, unmarked N/A pages or incomplete packages; no documents accepted after the response due date.
Risk: proposals are subject to public disclosure even if marked confidential, and the County is not liable for any disclosure.
Risk: proposer must hold the County harmless from liability of any nature or kind for infringement of patent, copyright or other proprietary rights.
